data.title: A TBK1/ULK1 signalling axis couples lysosomal stress to TFEB activation.
data.authors: Esposito A; Bayramoglu I; Varriale C; Cavaliere MP; Brunetti ME; Agostinis R; Jansen RM; Tudorica DA; Duan Y; Spacci M; Calcagnì A; Strobl CD; Passerini V; Andreone F; Monfregola J; Richter J; Sacco F; Klapper W; Weigert O; Ballabio A; Zoncu R; Hurley JH; Dengjel J; Napolitano G

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.model_system: Human cell lines; ATP6V1B2-mutant follicular lymphoma patient samples
data.finding: Identifies a nutrient-independent lysosomal pathway in which v-ATPase recruits TBK1/ULK1 to phosphorylate FNIP1, inhibiting the FLCN:FNIP complex and releasing TFEB for nuclear translocation; recurrent ATP6V1B2 mutations found in follicular lymphoma patients constitutively hyperactivate this axis, driving TFEB-dependent tumor proliferation.
data.abstract_excerpt: Lysosomal adaptation to environmental changes is critical for cellular and metabolic homeostasis and requires coordination by the mTORC1 kinase, which conveys nutritional and stress signals into distinct, substrate-specific outputs. The FLCN-FNIP complex (FLCN:FNIP) serves as a crucial regulator of lysosomal function by selectively controlling the ability of mTORC1 to inhibit transcription factor EB (TFEB), a master regulator of catabolic programs and a known oncogene. Yet how FLCN:FNIP activity is regulated has remained unclear.
